en: *Abhidhānottara* 2:
A = Mānabaja Bajrācārya, E 29260 = NGMPP E 1517/7;
B = Śatapiṭaka edition.
Then the Blessed One, Vajrasattva, having entered the great wrathful absorption named "The Transformation of the Dharmadhātu," proclaimed the secret of all accomplishments.
with bodhisattva mahāsattvas as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably unspeakable Buddha-fields;
such as Rūpeśvaravajra and Mahāvīra.
And by the great hero Vedanāvajra;
and by the great hero Saṃjñāvajra;
and by the great hero Saṃskāravajra.
And by the great hero Vijñānavajra;
and by the great hero Sarvatathāgatadharmadhātuprabhuvajra;
and by the great hero Mohavajra.
And by the great hero Śrotravajra;
and by the great hero Ghrāṇavajra;
and by the great hero Jihvāvajra.
And by the Great Hero Mātsaryavajra;
and by the Great Hero Sarvatathāgataiśvaryavajra;
and by the Great Hero Pṛthivīvajra.
And by the great hero Water-Vajra,
and by the great hero Fire-Vajra,
and by the great hero Wind-Vajra.
Together with the Great Hero Ākāśadhātuvajra and others led by him,

he dwelt within the assembly circle arising from the secret heart and the bhaga, which pervades the infinite, boundless, and entirely exhaustive realm of phenomena (dharmadhātu), amidst various supreme great samaya circles and the three secrets.
And by the great hero Khaṇḍakapālivajra,
and by the great hero Mahākaṅkālavajra,
and by the great hero Kaṅkālavajra.
And by the great hero Vikaṭadaṃṣṭravajra,
and by the great hero Surāvairivajra,
and by the great hero Amitābhavajra.
And by the great hero Vajraprabha;
and by the great hero Vajradeha;
and by the great hero Vajrāṅkura.
And by the great hero Vajrajaṭila,
and by the great hero Mahāvīravajra,
and by the great hero Vajrahūṃkāra.
And by the great hero Subhadravajra;
and by the great hero Vajragarbha;
and by the great hero Bhadra.
And by the great hero Mahābhairavavajra;
and by the great hero Virūpākṣavajra;
and by the great hero Mahāsattvavajra.
And by the great hero Ratnavajra;
and by the great hero Hayavajra;
and by the great hero Ākāśagarbhavajra.
And by the great hero Herukavajra;
and by the great hero Padmanarteśvara;
and by the great hero Vairocanavajra.
And he was seen by Vajrasattva, the Great Hero,
and by all the supreme Tathāgatas who filled the entire realm of desire, headed by these very ones.

Then the Blessed One entered the meditative absorption called "The Equality of Non-duality of the Vajra-Samaya of All Clan Lords," and proclaimed this Great Samaya—the union of the non-dual assembly of the Heroines and Heroes of the Secret Yoga, arising from the secret state, which is the secret samaya of his own [nature]: AU 2.4. ||
They are as follows:
the great yoginī named Pātanī,
and the great yoginī named Māraṇī.
The great yoginī named Ākarṣaṇī;
the great yoginī named Nartteśvarī;
the great yoginī named Padmajvālanī.
The one named Ḍākinī is a great yoginī; the one named Lāmā is a great ḍākinī;
the one named Khaṇḍarohā is a great ḍākinī.
The great vajra-ḍākinī named Rūpiṇī;
the great yoginī named Pracaṇḍā; the great yoginī named Caṇḍākṣī.
The great yoginī named Prabhāmatī;
the great yoginī named Mahānāsā;
the great yoginī named Vīramatī.
The great yoginī named Kharvarī; the great yoginī named Laṅkeśvarī;
the great yoginī named Drumacchāyā.
The great yoginī named Airāvatī;
the great yoginī named Mahābhairavā;
the great yoginī named Vāyuvegā.
The great yoginī named Surābhakṣī;
the great yoginī named Śyāmādevī; the great yoginī named Subhadrā.
The great yoginī named Hayakarṇā; the great yoginī named Khagānanā;
the great yoginī named Cakravegā.
The great yoginī named Khaṇḍarohā; the great yoginī named Sauṇḍinī;
the great yoginī named Cakravartinī.
The great yoginī named Suvīrā;
the great yoginī named Mahābalā;
the great yoginī named Cakravartinī.

The great yoginī named Mahāvīryā, headed by such [deities], appeared in the sky throughout the infinite and boundless realms, accompanied by all the heroes and yoginīs who were filled with the essence of compassion, uttering various forms of *hūṃ*, *phaṭ*, and *kilikilā* sounds, and engaged in the embraces and kisses of their own samaya. Having seen this, the supreme vow of the heroes was remembered; the vow of the glorious Vajraḍāka was remembered. The vow of the glorious Vajraḍāka is that which arises from the non-dual gnosis of the ḍākinīs Vajravārāhī and the others; it is the emergence of the Perfection of Wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*).
Then the Blessed One proclaimed the secret of the entire family of the host of Mothers.
Namely:
the Vajramātṛ named Kākāsyā (Crow-faced),
and the Vajramātṛ named Ullukāsyā (Owl-faced).
She named Śvānāsyā is a mother of the Vajra; she named Śūkarāsyā is a mother of the Vajra;
she named Yamadāḍhī is a mother of the Vajra.
The Mother of Vajra named Yamadūtī;
the Mother of Vajra named Yamadaṃṣṭrī;
the Mother of Vajra named Yamamathanī.

With these as their leaders, [the assembly] filled the entire expanse of space with hosts of mothers and fathers, gave the pledge of the Great Vajra Family—the pledge consisting of Śrī Heruka and Prajñāpāramitā, whose nature is the non-dual wisdom of the utterly pure *dharmadhātu* of all the Lords of the Families:
"All phenomena are indeed non-existent, devoid of the characteristics of phenomena;
born from the selflessness of phenomena—this is the supreme method of the pledge. Thus it was said.
Then the Blessed One proclaimed the vajra-samaya named "The Non-duality of the Vajra Armor."
Namely:
by Vajrasattva, the great lord of yoga;
and by Padmanarteśvara, the great lord of yoga.
And by Vajraheruka, the great lord of yoga;
and by Vajrasūrya, the great lord of yoga;
and by Paramāśva, the great lord of yoga.

Then, one should recollect that supreme secret of the great samaya, which is the non-duality of wisdom and means—the ultimate reality of the non-dual supreme protection consisting of the six families, the six-limbed placement (ṣaḍaṅganyāsa), and the observance (samaya).
She who is named Vajravārāhī is the Vajrayoginī; she who is named Yāminī is the Mahāyogeśvarī;
she who is named Mohinī is the Mahāyogeśvarī.
The great mistress of yoga named Saṃcālinī; the great mistress of yoga named Saṃtrāsanī;
the great mistress of yoga named Caṇḍikā.

Thus, moreover, the space-element and the dharma-element are non-dual and equal. This is the great secret heart-mantra of the yoga of protection. In this manner, many kinds of yoginīs offered edible foods held up with their own hands; [among these] the best is that which is freshly prepared while warm.

Then, having entered the samādhi called "The Vajra Expanded by the Great Samaya of the Names of Various Mantras," and seeing this [world] as if filled with the entire, exhaustive realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*), he was seen filling the pores of his own body and the various assemblies of diverse qualities with various means of discipline (*vinaya*).

The Blessed One, who perceives the welfare of sentient beings, who possesses the mountain of the Vidyādharas named Sakalapati, and who is variegated by the bliss of non-dual yoga through the flavor of great compassion and wrath, displayed a great miracle for the sake of those to be converted, demonstrating his sovereignty over the entire triple world.

Above the realms of Varuṇa, Agni, Vāyu, and Mahendra, he fashioned a great palace named *Mahāprāsāda-maṇḍalarāja-śrīvajrasattva-dharmadhātu-spharaṇa-mahākrodhābhyudaya* (The Great Arising of the Wrathful One, the Pervasion of the Dharmadhātu of Śrīvajrasattva), adorned with various splendors of diverse jewels from the king of mountains, Sumeru, the best of peaks. Upon its summit, the great assembly (*mahāvajraparṣad*) arising from the Great Samantabhadra gathered and took their seats.

Adorned with various, manifold, and diverse vajra-ornaments of exquisite beauty, embellished with moon and sun motifs, and further graced with bells, chowries, banners, networks of tinkling bells, tassels, and upper-tiered arches; [they are] endowed with the vows of yoga, such as the turning of the wheel of Dharma by means of threads made of vajra.

[It was filled] with various gods, nāgas, yakṣas, rākṣasas, bhūtas, pretas, piśācas, those possessed by madness, epilepsy, and planetary seizures, as well as the wicked and the extremely wicked; with vetālas, corpses, jackals, crickets, frogs, and vīra-ḍākinīs, resounding with the sounds of "phetkāra" and "lalata"; adorned with the dancing of headless trunks (kabandhas) accompanied by the sounds of bells and hand-drums; and [filled] with the graceful movements of the attendants of Vajrapāṇi, who have descended through their skill to bring benefit and compassion to all sentient beings.

When their dance of the *kavalāvarta* was performed, [the Lord] formed his hands in the gesture of reverence (*añjali*) while seated in the *ālīḍha* posture. With palms joined, he requested the Blessed One, the Buddha-Kāpālika, to teach the Dharma of the supreme, most profound method—the Great Vajra Wrathful King—possessing a majestic and great form, with a deep voice, within the circle of his own assembly, through the nets of the *Ḍākinīsaṃvararāja* known as the *Abhidhānottara*.
"Teach well, teach well through various instructions on the Dharma and by indicating all the diverse gateways! Listen, O beloved Vajrapāṇi, regarding the Mahāyāna."
The second chapter, the Chapter on the Prayer, from the Abhidhānottara.
